summary: Number 19 of the Summation of United States Army Military Government Activities in Korea covers April 1947. Politically, the Military Governor restated the policy of Koreanization, the Interim Legislative Assembly amended and passed the summer-grain collection program, took up local self-government, a provisional constitution and a bill against collaborators, and Syngman Rhee returned to a mass welcome while Lyuh Woon Heung launched the Laboring Masses Party. Secretary of State Marshall's letter proposing that the U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission reconvene was printed in full with Molotov's reply naming 20 May. Economically, coal and silk output rose, seven New Korea Company subsidiaries went to the Department of Commerce, prices of cloth and grain fell, imports from Japan are tabulated, and the controlled-commodity list grew. Social sections cover cholera immunization, refugees from the North at about 3,000 a day, adult literacy and radio and press. Historians will find detailed statistics and verbatim documents.
highlights: The Military Governor's policy statement said Americans would withdraw to advisory and inspectorial positions, and Ordinance No. 135 of 15 March 1947 gave Koreans full responsibility for appointment to public office.

The Legislative Assembly adopted six amending articles to the summer-grain collection program, limiting collection to one fifth of production and forbidding forcible methods, and on 4 April voted 42 to 0, with 12 abstentions, to have the National Food Administration carry it out.

On 21 April Kim Fung Chun presented a draft provisional constitution of seven chapters and 67 sections, with the Assembly serving as the Provisional Government, and a bill defining traitors, collaborators, war criminals and profiteers had its first reading on 22 April.
Secretary of State Marshall's letter of 14 April asked that the Joint Commission be reconvened; Molotov replied proposing it resume in Seoul on 20 May and report in July-August 1947.

Lyuh Woon Heung founded the Laboring Masses Party (preparatory committee of 38 on 7 April, platform 26 April), while Kim Koo and the Chungking group resigned from the Korean Independence Party's committees.

March anthracite output was 26,876 metric tons against a 29,500-ton quota; raw silk reached a 1947 peak of 61,707 pounds, and seven New Korea Company subsidiaries moved to the Department of Commerce on 1 April.
Tai Han No Chong won the Seoul Electric Company bargaining election on 19 April with 3,260 of 3,805 votes cast, and Ordinance No. 139 raised tax-delinquency penalties up to 30 percent from 19 April.

Refugees from North Korea entered at roughly 3,000 a day at Tongduchon-ni; the Department of Public Health and Welfare received a 8,450,000 yen grant, and 222 South Koreans were repatriated from 31 March to 27 April.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers, title page for No. 19 (April 1947), table of contents of four parts, and list of 17 charts plus a map of Korea.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: Assembly action on grain collection and the constitution, the Marshall letter, economic and social highlights.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Assembly passed the summer-grain program on 4 April; draft constitution presented 21 April; Laboring Masses Party announced; Marshall and Molotov letters summarized.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: March coal highest of the fiscal year, raw silk peak of 61,707 pounds, seven subsidiaries moved to Commerce, mail to China resumed 4 April, controlled list expanded.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Cholera immunization in port cities, typhoid down to 707 cases, 8,450,000 yen for northern refugees, literacy of 1,169,863 in Kyongsang-namdo.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government policy, civil service, the Legislative Assembly's work, party politics, the Joint Commission correspondence, and law, fire and security matters.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Policy of Koreanization, civil-service exams, Assembly debate on grain collection, local self-government, constitution and collaborator bills, party developments, Marshall and Molotov letters.

sections.title: Administration and Korean Civil Service
sections.summary: Military Governor's statement on Koreanization and Ordinance No. 135; 155 of 232 clerk candidates passed the civil-service examination on 18 April.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Six amending articles on summer-grain collection, rice-export rumor probe, six-tier local government bill, child labor ordinance, 67-section constitution, new members bringing total to 90, collaborator bill.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: National Society convention 19-20 April and Rhee's report, Kim Koo group resigns from the Korean Independence Party, Lyuh Woon Heung's Laboring Masses Party, boycott by the Independent Labor and Farmer Party.

sections.title: U. S.-U. S. S. R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: Full text of Marshall's letter of 14 April and Molotov's reply proposing the Commission resume in Seoul on 20 May 1947.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: By 5 April the Office of Foreign Affairs had authorized 841 Japanese women married to Koreans to stay in South Korea.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: No major disturbances; fires rose from 192 to 250 with 137,835,144 yen damage in February; prison wardens met 24-26 April; 250 Constabulary cadets commissioned.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources, industry, commerce and finance, and rationing and price control, with provincial and commodity statistics.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: New Korea Company's vested-land sale proposal, 1946 livestock census of 637,085 cattle, March coal output of 26,876 tons, 20,000,000 yen copper fund.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Seven New Korea Company subsidiaries transferred 1 April, Hokusen Paper Mill shut for pulp shortage, 8,461 bales of Japanese cotton, Seoul Electric Company union election.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Bank of Chosen notes at 17,239,535,835 yen, Ordinance No. 139 tax penalties, revenue totals, imports from Japan, locomotives and streetcars, postal and radio communications.

sections.title: Finance and Revenues
sections.summary: Currency up slightly, gold at 1,400 yen per momme, Ahn Chai Hong's tax appeal, Monopoly Bureau 69.4 percent of revenue to 31 March.

sections.title: Government Monopolies and Property Control
sections.summary: Salt shortage survey, 13 of 25 saltern engineer candidates passed, 180 Japanese property liquidations processed.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: 4,243 tons of Burmese rice on 15 April, Japanese textiles, machinery and coal (48,985 tons in April), metals promised to the United States.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 38 American locomotives imported, 16,733 freight cars moved in March, only 48 streetcars running daily, Seoul waterworks expansion.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: First large mail shipment to China 4 April, postal savings of 6,981,049 depositors, wire traffic up 148 percent, radio transmitters and technical school.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Summer-grain quotas, rent-in-kind change on 26 March, controlled list expanded 17 April, leather prices set, prices of cloth down 30 percent.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and refugees, education and youth organizations, and information programs including film, radio and press.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Typhoid fell from 1,409 to 707, 4,633 licensed physicians, 3,000 refugees a day at Tongduchon-ni, 222 repatriated and 6,122 Chinese registered.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Seoul National University extension credit, music festivals, adult literacy, Youth Movement at 66,722 members, Boston Marathon celebration, eight missionaries returned.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Health and current-events films, 341 hours of March broadcasting, and press reaction to Rhee's 27 April welcome and the Laboring Masses Party.

sections.title: Map of Korea
sections.summary: Foldout map of Korea closing the issue, as listed in the charts index.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: University of Virginia Alderman Library due-date slip (due 14 January 1949), blank pages and scan end sheets.
